subject: Literature
title: William Wordsworth and Nature Poetry
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on William Wordsworth and Nature Poetry.

hook.text: Wordsworth declared that poetry should use 'the real language of men,' not the ornate style of the aristocracy.

buildup.text: His 1798 Lyrical Ballads, written with Coleridge, launched the Romantic movement in English literature.

discovery.text: He found spiritual transcendence in nature: daffodils, mountains, and lakes became as sacred as any cathedral.

twist.text: As a young man he supported the French Revolution, but he became deeply conservative as he aged, disappointing his admirers.

climax.text: Wordsworth taught poets that ordinary experience, observed with intense feeling, was poetry's true subject matter.

punchline.text: He found the sublime in a field of daffodils.

quiz.question: What did Wordsworth believe poetry should use?
options: Ornate classical language and mythological references
The real language of ordinary men and women
